overview.intro: BCom is a 3-year undergraduate course for students who have cleared 12th standard with a major in Commerce. The full form of BCom is Bachelor of Commerce. BCom Admissions are based on merit as well as entrance exams such as CUET, PU CET, NPAT, etc. BCom offers diverse Career options in the fields of Finance, Banking, and Accounting, making it a popular choice for commerce students after class 12. On an average, the BCom course fee ranges from INR 20,000 to INR 1,00,000.

Entrance Exams: Some universities and colleges, like Delhi University, admit students to the B.Com course based on their marks in national or state-level entrance exams like CUET, IPU CET and NPAT.
Candidates must have completed and passed class 12 or the equivalent from a recognized board.

The minimum percentage for B.Com admission varies from college to college. Delhi University's cutoff for BCom admission ranges in the area of 99%, whereas, for some colleges, it can be a minimum of 45%.
Students from any stream can apply for B.Com admission, but a candidate can get preference over candidates from other streams if he/she/zee has completed 10+2 with Commerce.
Some colleges conduct entrance examinations for admissions to B.Com. Candidates qualifying in BCom Entrance Exams are given admission based on marks secured in these examinations.

faq.question: Ques. Can you do a BCom course without mathematics?
faq.answer: Ans. No, a candidate should have mathematics as a compulsory subject for studying a BCom course.

faq.question: Ques. What is the difference between a BCom Honours and a BCom general degree?
faq.answer: Ans. In BCom (Honours), students are required to study extra subjects so as to earn additional credits. These additional credits play a major role in applying for higher studies, where Universities prefer students with honours to regular students. The honours degree can also aid in employment opportunities for specific domains, such as Computer Applications, Data science, Human Resources, etc.

faq.question: Ques. How to get admission to BCom in Delhi University in 2025?
faq.answer: Ans. BCom admission to Delhi University will now be based on CUET scores. The exam will be held in multiple phases and will begin in July 2025.

faq.question: Ques. Which course is good BBA or BCom? Which course should one opt for in intermediate, and which is better for an MBA in the future?
faq.answer:
Ans. BBA and BCom courses are good, but it depends upon whether the candidate wants to specialize in a particular domain and do BCom Honours or wants to have an overview of all the subjects in the field of commerce.

Ques. Which colleges in DU offer BCom Hons without math?

Ans. Every college at Delhi University offers B.Com (Hons) without including math in your best four, despite the fact that math should be a subject in your 12th grade. It is to take into account that to be admitted to an undergraduate course that requires a specific subject or a group of subjects, candidates must have passed the subject/each of the subjects individually.

The procedure is as follows:

faq.question: Ques. Can I study BCom online?
faq.answer: Ans. Yes, you can pursue a Bachelor of Commerce (BCom) degree online through flexible distance learning programs offered by various universities and online platforms in India, such as IGNOU, the University of Mysore, and others recognized by the UGC-DEB. These programs provide the same core curriculum as on-campus degrees, including accounting, finance, and economics, while allowing students to study at their own pace from anywhere with an internet connection.

Most of the students prefer to pursue BCom (Hons) program as it helps to prepare for certification exams such as Chartered Accountancy (CA) and other certifications side by side or afterwards. Delhi University is highly known and famous for its BCom (Hons.) course. faq.question: Ques. Is BCom Hons tough?
faq.answer: Ans. If we are comparing BCom Honours course to simple BCom, then we can say it is slightly tougher, but it provides a great platform and required knowledge to pursue many professional courses such as CA, CMA, CFA, CFP, etc.

faq.question: Ques. Is it better to do CA after BCom Hons or with BCom Hons?
faq.answer: Ans. It totally depends upon you. If you can manage both the studies, then definitely you should do it. But most of the time, students find it exhausting and prefer to pursue CA after the course completion.

faq.question: Ques. Which is better, BCom or BBA?
faq.answer:
Ans. Both these courses are one of the highly pursued and regarded courses in their respective field. Students who eventually want to pursue MBA or any other master level management course, then you should pursue BBA. But if you want to pursue CA, CFA, ACCA or any other finance or accounting certification then you should pursue BCom Honours, rather than BBA.


In terms of salary, BBA graduates get a slightly better salary compensation than BCom Hons graduates.

faq.question: Ques. What is the cut off for BCom (Hons) at St. Xavier’s, Kolkata?

The passing criteria is pretty simple. You are only required to secure a minimum of 40% in all the subjects of that particular academic year in total.

Accountant may have additional responsibilities if employed by an accounting firm. They prepare tax returns and financial statements, and accounting firms represent clients on matters pertaining to their financial affairs. It is the staff Accountant’s responsibility to meet with clients to discuss their financial matters, equipment, real property, and tax liability. INR 2,64,000

Cashier Cashiers help customers select the right product, much like retail sales workers. They greet customers as they enter the store, answer questions about products. They assist in locating desired items and encourage the customer to buy the merchandise. They may also set up store displays and perform cashier duties. Formal education is usually not required to work in this field, but companies that sell more technical items may prefer a candidate with a high school diploma. The training is generally offered by the employer. INR 1,77,000

Insurance manager Actuaries that work in the insurance industry generally specialize in either life and health insurance or property and casualty insurance. Integral role that an Actuary performs in insurance companies stems from their risk assessment research. Research helps them forecast how likely it is for certain risk events to occur and how these events will impact their company with potential loss. An Insurance Actuary with a property and casualty specialization might calculate how many claims the company can expect to have as a result of car accidents. They must also weigh an insured person's vehicle age, type, sex and driving history to devise a premium that is competitive with other insurance companies. INR 6,13,000

Loan counselor A Loan Counsellor works for a financial institution, processes a client's application materials, verifies the information and works with the client to come up with a financial plan. They explain the types and rate terms of loans available, and generate the legal paperwork necessary to complete the loan process. They also answer questions about existing loans and assist struggling clients by rescheduling payments or restructuring loans to help them remain solvent. INR 2,02,000

Financial Advisor A Financial Advisor may also be called a Financial Planner. There may be no official requirements for financial advisors; employers prefer those who have a college education. Colleges and universities offer undergraduate and graduate degree programs in financial advising. Some degrees in business, accounting or finance are also recommended for those entering this field. Coursework in financial advising programs often includes retirement planning, investing tactics, and insurance. Graduates need to take advanced math courses, and classes in economics and interpersonal relations. Graduate programs offer internships at banks and other financial firms where students can gain valuable real-life experience needed for the position. INR 4,24,000

faq.question: Ques. What is BCom bank management?

The candidates also gain expertise in different banking operations such as deposits, credit distribution, recurring deposits, savings, demat account, etc.

faq.question: Ques. How can I start banking?
faq.answer: Ans. You can start your career in banking by taking up relevant streams after the completion of 12th. The candidates should preferably be from commerce background so that they have a relatively stronger base in accounting and finance and ideas about credit and debit. After completion of graduation, apply for the SBI and IBPS exam to land jobs in the government banks.

faq.question: Ques. How can I get a bank job with no experience?
faq.answer: Ans. Government banks often do not require the candidates to have experience in banking. However, they would have to crack the entrance exam such as SBI PO, SBI Clerk or IBPS Clerk to land a job in a government bank. In case of private banks candidates are often recruited through campus placement

faq.question: Ques. What Is BCom in banking and finance?
faq.answer: Ans. It is a 3 years graduation program that increases the candidates knowledge in financial statements, accounting principles and banking operation.

faq.question: Ques. Which degree is required for a bank manager?
faq.answer: Ans. Candidates with B.Com or BBA Degree can become a bank manager. However, candidates with MBA (In Finance, Banking) are mainly preferred for the role of a bank manger.

faq.question: Ques. Is maths compulsory for bank manager?
faq.answer: Ans. Yes, a bank manager must have good knowledge in maths because the daily operational activities require them to analyse various reports as well as financial statements. Also the entrance exams such as IBPS and SBI have question related to the arithmetic section, making maths a compulsory subject for candidates who aspires to be bank manger.

faq.question: Ques. What are the BCom Financial Markets Subjects?
faq.answer: Ans. The BFM course covers key essentials of the operational and functional nature of financial markets, stock trading and exchanges, debt markets, equity markets, corporate finance, microeconomics, macroeconomics, risk management, etc.

faq.question: Ques. Is BFM recommended to become a CFA (Chartered Financial Analyst)?
faq.answer: Ans. BFM is the perfect undergraduate program for students planning to pursue C.F.A. Projects, case studies, presentations, mock trials, replica stock, and industry visits guarantee that the course offers a solid mix of theory and practice.

faq.question: Ques. Do we need math for BFM?
faq.answer: Ans. BFM includes accounts and statistics, which in turn involves math. Math is therefore the basis of finance. Therefore, any aspirant must have the basic mathematical knowledge/ skill.

faq.question: Ques. Is BAF better than BFM?
faq.answer: Ans. Both the courses include similar financial studies, career opportunities and higher studies options. The only difference is that BFM provides detailed knowledge about finance, market, and a broader scope for investment compared to BAF, which only teaches financing, and accounting.

faq.question: Ques. Can a Bachelor in Financial Markets work in a bank?
faq.answer: Ans. Definitely, Right after finishing BFM, graduates can join an accounting firm and start working as Accounting Assistants, Financial Planner, Stock Brokers and so on.

faq.question: Ques. What is the average salary for BFM?
faq.answer: Ans. The average beginning yearly salary for a BFM graduate ranges from Rs. 4 lakh to Rs. 6 lakh. It may vary from company to company and depending on the role.

faq.question: Ques. What is the average fee for BFM?
faq.answer: Ans. The average fee is about INR 50,000 per year and might increase due to the rise in the increase of the courses in many colleges.

faq.question: Ques. Does BFM come under BBA or BCOM?
faq.answer: Ans. BFM is not similar to BBA and B.com. BFM is the latest course put in for the commerce students. The Bachelor of Financial Markets is a specialised degree in commerce that helps the students to understand the various aspects of financial markets, enabling them to understand economics, finance, markets, and risks in a clearer way.

faq.question: Ques. Can we do MBA after BFM?
faq.answer: Ans. Yes, you can do an MBA after BFM. The University of Mumbai had begun the Bachelor of Commerce (Financial Markets) course in 2008. The course was created not only to aim at training students in their academics but also in the ever changing field of Financial Market but also leads to the all-round improvement of their personality.

faq.question: Ques. What are the top jobs that you can do after completing BFM?
faq.answer: Ans. Chartered Accountant (CA), Financial Risk Manager (FRM), MBA in Finance, Chartered Finance Analyst (CFA), and Company Secretary (CS) are some of the major jobs, which can be done after completing BFM.

faq.question: Ques. Which is the highest paid job after BFM?
faq.answer: Ans. One of the highest paid jobs after completing BFM is the Investment Banker. The average salary of an investment banker can reach upto 46,17,413 INR per year.

faq.question: Ques. Is doing a B.Com worth it?
faq.answer: Ans. Definitely Yes. In present times, business administration, business management, entrepreneurship are some of the most popular career options among the young generation. Now, B.Com can certainly provide you with the skill set and knowledge you need to pursue these careers. So, if you are concerned about the career options you're gonna get after completing B.Com, we can say that there are plenty of options waiting on the other side of a B.Com degree.

faq.question: Ques. Do I necessarily have to give an entrance exam to get admitted to B.Com?
faq.answer: Ans. No. Some colleges and universities have their own entrance examinations which one has to clear to be eligible to get admitted in B.Com or any other program. But, there are other colleges and universities which give admission to students completely on the basis of merit. It basically depends on the college or university that you want to get admitted to, whether you would have to give an entrance examination or not.

faq.question: Ques. Is B.Com divided into 8 semesters or 6?
faq.answer: Ans- B.Com is a 3-year undergraduate program, which is divided into 6 semesters.

faq.question: Ques. Can I become a teacher after completing B.Com?
faq.answer: Ans. Yes. But, you would have to complete the B.Ed program after B.Com to become a teacher.

faq.question: Ques. Should I do M.Com after completing B.Com?
faq.answer: Ans. Higher educational qualification is always good. Especially when it comes to getting a job, a M.Com degree certainly can help you better than a B.Com degree. So, there is no problem in doing M.Com after completing B.Com.

faq.question: Ques. Can Science stream students also pursue B.Com in India?
faq.answer: Ans. Yes, students from Science stream can also pursue B.Com in India after completing 12th. Though, candidates must have the minimum marks required to get into the B.Com program. The minimum marks required to get into the program can vary from college to college.

faq.question: Ques. Is Mathematics necessary for B.Com?
faq.answer: Ans. In India Mathematics is necessary to get admission only in the B.Com (Hons) program. But yes, basic and some advanced knowledge of Mathematics can surely benefit the students throughout the B.Com program.

faq.question: Ques.  What is the difference between B.Com and B.Com (Hons) programs?
faq.answer: Ans. There aren't many differences between these two programs. Basically the B.Com program is designed to give the students an overall education in Commerce. But, in the B.Com (Hons) program one can specialize in any branch or subject of Commerce like, Finance, Accounting, Banking etc.

faq.question: Ques. What is better, B.Com or BBA?
faq.answer: Ans. It will actually depend on what you want to become. But, if you are worried about scopes then we can assure you that there are plenty of scopes in both the lines. After studying B.Com you can make a career in Banking, Commerce, Finances, Accounting, Business etc. On the other hand, after completing BBA it will be easy for you to make a career in Business Management.

faq.question: Ques. Is it possible to pursue an MBA degree after B.Com?
faq.answer: Ans. Of course, it is possible to pursue an MBA degree after B.Com. In fact it has been one of the most famous recent career options among the students who have just completed B.Com to pursue an MBA degree further.

faq.question: Ques. How is the placement post completion of BCom International Business?

B.Com. Statistics is not just theoretical but it also has certain practical subjects. It is a 6 semester course programme with some colleges following the credit system.

The science of collecting, maintaining, evaluating, interpreting, and presenting numerical and categorical data is known as statistics. The B.Com. is a bachelor's degree in business administration. Actuarial Science, Applied Information Economics, Biostatistics, Business Statistics, Data Analysis, Demography, Econometrics, and other specific topics are covered in the (Statistics) degree programme for the holistic development of the students.

The advanced education programme covers topics such as analysis, probability theory, statistical methods, database management systems, and so on. The degree programme is important in the financial area.
Anyone with an ample interest in statistics and economics and is looking for a career in accounts, data interpretation, etc can go for this course.

After completing a B.Com. (Statistics) degree programme, students can pursue higher education (M.Com., MBA, etc.) or pursue a career in banking, insurance, finance, auditing, or accountancy in both the public and private sectors.
Those with a B.Com. (Statistics) degrees are most prepared for entry-level positions in banking, insurance, and other financial services.

The B.Com. (Statistics) degree serves as a foundation for future studies in this discipline, such as M.A., Ph.D., and M.Phil. Degrees in Statistics, which upon completion qualify one for a teaching position at any university or college.
Those with a B.Com. (Statistics) degree has a lot of work options because statisticians are needed everywhere there is data, and practically every organization needs well-formulated and ordered data.
A student with a B.Com. (Statistics) degree is eligible to take the Indian Statistical Services, Indian Economic Services, and Indian Civil Services exams.
Students must have completed and passed an intermediate level course (10+2) in one of the following subjects: accounting, business studies, economics, or mathematics.
Some prestigious institutions and institutes need a minimum of 50% in the above topics at the 10+2 level.

Candidates must provide the required documents in the correct format and pay the application fees after finishing the registration process.
They administer an Entrance Test to assess a candidate's skills and ability to think critically.
Following these rounds, selected candidates are notified via email or a merit list is prepared based on their aptitude, talents, and the amount of seats available in that specific college.

faq.question: Ques. Is BCom a good choice post high school?
faq.answer: Ans. Yes, BCom is a fundamental, theoretical-oriented and specialised degree (being in travel and tourism) which allows you to create a good grasp of the fundamental foundation you have studied so far. It definitely starts up your career opportunities/average pay.

faq.answer: Ans. The Average salary of BCom graduates in India varies between INR 3,00,000 to as high as 5,00,000 per annum.
